$meta.name: MyChama Firestore Data Contract
$meta.purpose: Single source of truth for the MyChama live build AND the SAMUHIA WhatsApp bot. Both are written against this file. If a field changes here it changes in both codebases in the same commit.

conventions.documentIds: Firestore auto-IDs everywhere except paymentIntents (doc ID = payment reference) and loanProducts (doc ID = product slug, e.g. flat_emergency). The demo's uid('ln') style IDs are NOT carried over — the document ID is the ID.
conventions.memberId: Always the members subcollection document ID. Every cross-reference (contributions.memberId, loans.memberId, mgrPots.memberIds[], transactions.memberId) stores that exact string.
conventions.uid: members.uid is the Firebase Auth UID when the member has an app account, else null. WhatsApp-only members are legitimate and always have uid: null.
conventions.dates: Calendar-day fields (paidOn, requestedOn, dueDate, joinDate, date) are ISO date strings 'YYYY-MM-DD' — string-sortable, which is what every range query in firestore.indexes.json relies on. Do not switch these to Timestamps without re-writing the indexes.
conventions.timestamps: createdAt / updatedAt are epoch milliseconds (number), for cheap numeric range filters and to match the bot's session clock.
conventions.money: All amounts are KES as numbers, rounded to 2dp. Never store money as a string. Fees are stored alongside the net amount, never subtracted from it.
conventions.phone: members.phone is display E.164 ('+254712345671'). members.phoneNormalized is the canonical lookup key produced by normalizePhone() — always E.164, always written on every create and update. The WhatsApp bot resolves membership solely via a collection-group query on phoneNormalized, so a stale value means a member silently loses WhatsApp access.
conventions.nationalId: members.idNumber holds the full number and must never be sent to a client (see firestore.rules). members.idLast4 is the last 4 digits, and is what the WhatsApp bot compares against as a second authentication factor. members.nationalIdMasked ('•••• 1234') is the display form.
conventions.arraysVsSubcollections: The demo nests mgrPot.records[] and mgrPot.paidOut[] as arrays. Live they are subcollections (mgrPots/{potId}/records, mgrPots/{potId}/payouts) because both grow without bound and would blow the 1 MiB document limit on a daily pot. loans.schedule[] stays an array: it is bounded by maxTerm (≤ 12 entries) and is always read and written whole.
conventions.singleWriter: Contribution, loan-schedule and MGR-record balances are mutated by exactly ONE writer: the Paystack webhook (for online money) or an admin action in the app (for cash). The WhatsApp bot never mutates a balance.

feeEngine.note: These constants MUST match functions/src/config/mychama.config.ts FEES in the bot. A member quoted one figure on WhatsApp and charged another in the app is the single worst bug this system can ship.
feeEngine.grossUpForFees: Money IN (contributions, loan repayments, MGR collections). gross = net / (1 - PAYSTACK_FEE_RATE - ourRate). If gross*PAYSTACK_FEE_RATE exceeds the cap, recompute as gross = (net + PAYSTACK_FEE_CAP) / (1 - ourRate) with paystackFee pinned at the cap. The member pays gross; exactly net reaches the chama.
feeEngine.disbursementCost: Money OUT (loan disbursement, MGR payout). Fees are added ON TOP of the principal and deducted from the chama balance; the recipient receives the full principal. totalDeducted = principal + paystackFee + ourFee.
feeEngine.freePlan: plan === 'free' disables online collection and payout entirely (markup rate null). Cash/manual recording stays free on every plan, including MGR draws and reordering.

plans.minutesQuotaNull: null means unlimited. Beyond quota, a minutes export costs KES 100.

contributionAmount.note: Default per-cycle contribution used when generating contribution documents.

settlementAccount.note: Display label only, e.g. 'M-Pesa Paybill •••521'. Never the raw account.

settlementSplitCode.note: Paystack split code. The bot refuses to raise a payment intent without it.

status.note: The bot skips suspended chamas during membership lookup.

uid.note: Firebase Auth UID, or null for WhatsApp-only members.

phoneNormalized.note: Collection-group indexed. MUST be recomputed on every phone edit.

isAdmin.note: Derived: role !== 'member'. Stored so rules avoid a second read.

idNumber.note: Full National ID. Rules deny client reads of this field's document to non-admins; strip it in any callable that returns member lists.

totalContributed.note: Denormalised sum of contributions.paidAmount. Recomputed by the webhook/admin action that applies a payment — never by the bot.

rate.note: flat → % per month. reducing → % per annum.

defaults.name: Emergency Loan
defaults.desc: Quick short-term loan. Interest charged once on the full amount.

defaults.name: Development Loan
defaults.desc: Larger loan for development needs. Interest falls as you repay.

contributions.note: One document per member per cycle, pre-generated by a scheduled function when a cycle opens. The bot lists documents whose status is pending/partial/overdue.

period.note: Human label as in the demo, e.g. 'Oct 2026'.

periodKey.note: ADDED FOR LIVE. The demo sorted periods by array order, which Firestore cannot do. Every ordering and range query uses this field.

statusRules.overdue: status was pending/partial and dueDate < today (set by a scheduled sweep, not on read)
statusRules.overflow: Excess beyond `amount` rolls to the member's next unpaid period in periodKey order; whatever remains increments members.creditBalance. This mirrors applyContributionPayment() in the demo exactly.

loans.botWriteScope: CREATE ONLY, and only with status 'pending_approval', approvals {chair:false,treasurer:false}, source 'whatsapp'. The bot never approves, disburses or marks an instalment paid.

scheduleMaths.flat: totalInterest = principal * (rate/100) * term; totalPay = principal + totalInterest; installment = totalPay / term; each row: principalPart = principal/term, interestPart = totalInterest/term, opening/closing walk down from totalPay.
scheduleMaths.reducing: r = (rate/100)/12; installment = r === 0 ? principal/term : principal*r*(1+r)^term / ((1+r)^term - 1); per row: interestPart = opening*r, principalPart = installment - interestPart, closing = opening - principalPart.
scheduleMaths.dueDates: dueDate of row i = start + (i+1)*30 days, where start is the disbursement date (or application date while pending). Kept at 30-day steps, exactly as the demo, so figures reconcile.

statusTransitions.approved: → active (on disbursement; sets disbursedOn, method, and re-bases every schedule dueDate from the disbursement date)
statusTransitions.active: → overdue (scheduled sweep: an unpaid row's dueDate has passed) | completed (every row paid)

loans.repaymentOverflow: A repayment applies to the earliest unpaid instalment, then spills forward row by row; any remainder increments members.creditBalance. Mirrors applyLoanPayment() in the demo.

transactions.note: The ledger. Written by the Paystack webhook and by admin cash-recording actions. The bot only reads it, to build statements.

amount.note: Net amount moved for/against the chama.

ref.note: Paystack reference, or CASH... for manual entries.

settled.note: Whether the money has reached the chama's settlement account.

intentId.note: paymentIntents document ID when the payment originated on WhatsApp.

memberIds.note: array-contains indexed — this is how the bot finds a member's pots.

queue.note: Payout order. Head of queue receives next.

autoDemoteLate.note: When true, closing a period re-sorts the queue by late score so chronic late payers drift backwards.

period.note: Current open period. The bot only ever collects for this period.

mgrPots.note: A pot with status 'draft' or drawDone false is not collectable — the bot shows an explanatory message instead of a pay option.

mgrRecords.note: SUBCOLLECTION — replaces the demo's pot.records[] array. One document per member per period.
mgrRecords.uniqueness: At most one document per (potId, memberId, period). Enforce with a transaction on write — closing a period creates 'missed' rows for everyone without one.

mgrPayouts.note: SUBCOLLECTION — replaces the demo's pot.paidOut[] array.

paymentIntents.documentId: The payment reference itself, so the webhook resolves it in one get() and a replayed webhook is naturally idempotent.
paymentIntents.botWriteScope: CREATE with status 'pending'; UPDATE only paystackMessage / status→'failed' when Paystack rejects the charge outright. Everything after that belongs to the webhook.

amount.note: NET — what must reach the chama.

expiresAt.note: createdAt + 30 minutes. A scheduled sweep marks anything still pending past this as 'expired'.

paymentIntents.referenceFormat: MCW-{chamaId}-{CNT|LNR|MGR}-{epochMs}-{6 random uppercase}. The MCW prefix marks WhatsApp origin; the webhook can branch on it without a lookup.

userChamas.note: Rules-support index. Security rules resolve an authenticated user's role in a chama with ONE get() against this path instead of scanning members. Also doubles as the app's 'my chamas' list on login. Written by a Firestore trigger on members create/update/delete — never by hand.

settlementAccountRequests.note: Changing where the chama's money lands is the highest-risk action in the product. It is a request needing a second officer's approval, never a direct edit.

whatsappAuditLog.note: Top-level, not under a chama, because failed authentication attempts happen before a chama is resolved. No client may read it — admin/BigQuery only.
whatsappAuditLog.retention: TTL policy on `at`, 180 days. Configure in the Firestore console (TTL is not expressible in firestore.indexes.json).

whatsappContract.identity: The bot trusts the WhatsApp-verified sender number to FIND candidate memberships, and the last 4 digits of the National ID to CONFIRM identity. Neither alone is sufficient. Three wrong attempts lock My Chama on that number for 15 minutes; the session re-verifies after 15 minutes idle.

on charge.success: Load chamas/{chamaId}/paymentIntents/{reference}. If missing or already status 'success', ACK and stop — this is the idempotency gate.

In one Firestore transaction: apply intent.amount to the target (contribution spill-forward, loan schedule spill-forward, or the MGR record for intent.potPeriod), recompute members.totalContributed and members.creditBalance, write the transactions document with grossAmount/paystackFee/ourFee copied from the intent and intentId set, and set the intent status to 'success'.
Send the member a WhatsApp confirmation via the SAMUHIA bot's send endpoint (optional but recommended).
on charge.failed: Set intent status to 'failed' with paystackMessage. Touch nothing else.
webhookDuties.amountCheck: Verify the Paystack event amount equals Math.round(intent.grossAmount * 100). A mismatch means a tampered or stale reference — log to whatsappAuditLog with outcome 'denied' and do not apply.

seedForEmulator.note: Minimal, self-consistent fixture for local development. IDs are literal so the bot's flows can be exercised end to end.

chamas/sunrise01/loanProducts/reducing_d.name: Development Loan
chamas/sunrise01/loanProducts/reducing_d.desc: Larger loan for development needs. Interest falls as you repay.
